meta.title: AIGC Serving — Independent Runs Across a Runtime Restart
meta.subtitle: Illustrative ordering and durations. All three Runs keep Workflow v1; no performance measurements are implied.

spans.name: Run A · Workflow v1
spans.detail: A generation job is accepted before the backend interruption.

spans.name: Wait for external result
spans.detail: Saved wait references survive restart. Waiting does not imply holding a local execution slot; the external job may still use provider resources.

spans.name: Run B · Workflow v1
spans.detail: A separate request progresses independently of Run A.

spans.name: Wait for external result
spans.detail: The accepted provider job is not blindly re-submitted after restart; use callback or supported provider status lookup.

spans.name: Run C · Workflow v1
spans.detail: This Run has committed READY work before the interruption.

spans.name: Saved READY work
spans.detail: Eligible work is discoverable from persisted records after restart. This span does not claim priority or quota admission is already implemented.

spans.name: Backend offline / restart
spans.detail: Illustrative fault window. Run records remain; accepted external generation can continue independently. This is not an error status on the three Runs.

cards.title: Concurrency
items: The Runs share one Workflow version, but their input, progress and output references remain separate.

cards.title: Waiting and recovery
items: Execution and provider waits occupy different spans. Resume eligible saved work and resolve original accepted jobs, retaining each bound version.

cards.title: Next construction step
items: Capacity-aware admission, quota policy and cost-aware scheduling are a later extension; this illustration is not a throughput benchmark.
